itens.t: Chinese university bought restricted Nvidia H200 chips, records show
itens.r: An investigative report reveals that a Chinese university linked to the People's Liberation Army has successfully acquired advanced Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips. The purchase highlights ongoing challenges in enforcing stringent U.S. export control measures against high-tech proliferation. Despite federal blacklists restricting access to cutting-edge hardware, procurement records confirm the transaction was completed. International trade experts warn that such acquisitions undermine Washington's strategy to maintain a technological edge in AI development.
itens.d:
An investigation reveals that Chinese entities accessed United States-restricted artificial intelligence technology, specifically Nvidia H200 chips, through a Chinese university. Records show the acquisition occurred despite stringent export control measures put in place by authorities.

The findings highlight ongoing challenges in enforcing export restrictions on advanced semiconductors. Entities in China continue to navigate around regulatory barriers to secure restricted high-performance hardware used for AI development.
itens.e:
Recent records show that a Chinese university successfully acquired United States-restricted Nvidia H200 chips, despite stringent export control measures put in place by authorities. This transaction comes to light through an investigation revealing how restricted artificial intelligence technology has reached entities within China.

This finding matters because it exposes the continuous hurdles faced by regulators in enforcing export restrictions on advanced semiconductors. One risk is that entities in China can consistently navigate around regulatory barriers to secure high-performance hardware, which is critical for ongoing artificial intelligence development.

What to watch next is whether authorities will tighten regulatory mechanisms or introduce new compliance measures to plug these loopholes. This situation suggests that technology supply chains and export enforcement strategies will face heightened scrutiny moving forward.

itens.r: Educational authorities in Seoul are training supervisors to detect artificial intelligence-enabled smart glasses ahead of nationwide college entrance examinations. The high-tech eyewear has raised concerns over sophisticated academic cheating methods.

Education authorities in Seoul are training staff to identify AI-powered smart glasses ahead of the upcoming College Scholastic Ability Test. Officials are concerned the devices could facilitate cheating while remaining difficult to distinguish from regular eyewear.

The Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education will deploy hundreds of trained personnel across exam sites to perform physical inspections. While radio-frequency detectors will not be used this year, authorities are considering such equipment for future exams.

itens.t: SpaceX prepares Starship Flight 15 for historic double-catch attempt
itens.r: SpaceX moved its Super Heavy booster to the launch pad ahead of the upcoming Starship Flight 15 mission. The company aims to execute a groundbreaking double-landing test at its Texas facility.
itens.d:
SpaceX is preparing for the launch of Starship Flight 15 from Starbase, Texas, scheduled for Friday, November 13. The mission aims to achieve the first-ever full recovery of an orbital rocket by landing both the spacecraft and the Super Heavy booster.

In addition to the historic double-catch attempt, the flight will deliver 26 new Starlink V3 satellites into orbit. Teams are completing final prelaunch preparations as the countdown continues.

itens.t: NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes complete Earth gravity assist
itens.r: Twin spacecraft designed to study Mars' plasma environment successfully performed a complex double gravity assist around Earth. The maneuver puts the mission on a direct trajectory toward the Red Planet.
itens.d:
NASA's twin ESCAPADE Mars probes have completed a crucial engine burn close to Earth following a looping trajectory. The spacecraft launched in November 2025 on a Blue Origin New Glenn rocket.

Due to initial launch delays, mission planners designed a loitering orbit to set the probes on a path toward the Red Planet. No previous NASA mission has utilized this specific trajectory.

itens.t: NASA scientists show how gravitational waves can reveal new worlds
itens.r: Researchers analyzing data for the upcoming LISA observatory demonstrated that gravitational waves can help detect exoplanets. This novel astronomical method opens new avenues for discovering distant celestial bodies.
itens.d:
NASA scientists have demonstrated how the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna observatory can utilize gravitational waves to discover new exoplanets. Two new studies detail how planets orbiting tightly bound white dwarf systems leave an imprint on gravitational wave signals.

The detection method could allow researchers to identify Jupiter-mass worlds thousands of light-years away. Findings from the research were published in The Astrophysical Journal.

itens.t: Nvidia under scrutiny: Can the AI giant survive without Jensen Huang?

However, an admitted relationship with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence has placed him at the center of a major controversy. The situation highlights the significant key-person risk facing major technology companies in the sector.

The CEO has been the target of an internal company investigation and previous scrutiny involving federal authorities. Meanwhile, China's foreign ministry dismissed the espionage accusations as unfounded.
